messages:
emma: Hey team — newbie question: my local app using the sandbox key sometimes returns 429s when I save files (auto-reload). Is sandbox supposed to be flaky?

kate: Welcome! Sandbox is throttled. Auto-reload can cause rapid reconnects that hit the per-minute bucket.

emma: Oh that makes sense. Any quick mitigation so I can keep iterating?

infra-bot: Typical mitigations: add debounce to file watcher, limit concurrent streams to 1-2, implement exponential backoff on 429s. Sandbox defaults: ~30 req/min, 3 concurrent streams, ~40k tokens/day (org may vary).

emma: Good tips. For CI, should I keep using sandbox or request a staging key? Nightly runs sometimes exhaust quota.

devx: Use sandbox for small tests. For nightly or heavy CI, request a temporary staging (hosted) key via /onboard-access with expected qps and IP ranges. Also consider the local mock (devx/local-mock) to avoid consuming quota.

emma: Thanks — last one: which env var name should I use in GitHub Actions?

kate: Use REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for sandbox and REDWOOD_HOSTED_KEY for staging/prod to keep secrets clear.

emma: Awesome, I'll debounce the watcher and open a ticket if nightly still fails. Thanks!
